metadata.description: An IP network: a prefix, its gateway, and how addresses on it are assigned. The layer-3 half of "which network", selectable independently of the layer-2 segment it usually rides. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): RFC 4632 CIDR and the public-cloud subnet abstract over every prefix with a gateway and an assignment mode, so a subnet is one deliverable any network provider carves.

zone.description: What kind of network this is — a governed network-zone term, for placement only (common-elements.schema.json `network_zone_ref`).

tier.description: How good this network is — a governed network_tier floor the provider reports (common-elements.schema.json `network_tier_ref`).

prefix.description: The IP network in CIDR (198.51.100.0/24, 2001:db8::/64). Required: a subnet without a prefix is a name, not a subnet.

ip_family.description: Address family. Derivable from `prefix`; carried only where a provider reports it independently, and a disagreement with the prefix is drift, never an override.

gateway_address.description: The default route off this subnet, as an address: the address belongs to the subnet, the device answering it is a NetworkGateway and may change. Absent means an isolated L3 network.

address_assignment.description: How a host on this subnet gets its address: `pool` (an IPAddressPool within the subnet hands one out, reserved before realization so an address can be held while the workload is still hypothetical), `dhcp`, `static`.

dns_servers.description: Resolvers offered to hosts on this subnet. Carried because a provider reports it with the subnet and a consumer cannot obtain it any other way.

prefix.description: The CIDR actually realized. Where the subnet was ALLOCATED from a larger prefix (the /28-from-a-/16 case), the requested size and the granted range differ, so what a consumer got is a realized fact rather than a restatement of intent.

gateway_address.description: The default route as realized — the address a host on this subnet actually uses.

usable_addresses.description: How many addresses are assignable. DERIVED from the prefix minus the reservations the provider makes (network, broadcast, and whatever the platform holds back — clouds commonly take several), which is why it is an output and not a stored field: only the realizing provider knows its own reservations.

relationships.name: segment
relationships.description: The layer 2 segment this subnet rides on, WHERE THERE IS ONE. Optional and 0..1 on purpose: the L2-to-L3 mapping is not concrete — one segment may carry several subnets, and a cloud provider may expose no segment at all. A consumer selecting a subnet is making a different request from a consumer selecting a segment, and this edge is what relates them without merging them.

relationships.name: network
relationships.description: The logical network (VPC analogue) this subnet belongs to, where the provider exposes one.

adopts.role: The prefix notation and the aggregation semantics — adopted by reference, never re-expressed.

adopts.version: AWS VPC subnet / Azure VNet subnet / GCP subnetwork (convergent de-facto model)
adopts.role: The cloud realization of an L3 network. Recorded so a cloud provider naturalizes into this class rather than a cloud-only branch. The VPC that CONTAINS such a subnet has no class yet, and `contained_by → VirtualNetwork` below is the on-prem attachment-point case rather than a VPC. Tracked separately: a subnet is useful without its container, and guessing the container's shape would be worse than leaving it open.

context.purpose: Give the layer 3 network a first-class identity, so a consumer can require an IP network without naming a segment, and an allocation pool has something to sit inside.
context.plain_description: The IP side of a network — the address range, the way out of it, and how hosts on it get an address. Usually paired with one VLAN, but not always, which is why it is its own thing.
use_when: A workload must land on a particular IP network, whatever segment carries it
An address pool needs an L3 network to belong to
A /28 is allocated from a larger prefix somebody else holds
not_for: The layer 2 segment — that is `VLAN`, and a subnet may not map to exactly one
Handing out individual addresses — that is `IPAddressPool` within this subnet
works_with: `VLAN` — the segment this subnet usually rides on, when there is one
`IPAddressPool` — the allocatable ranges within this subnet
